# Guided walk card — 12 May 2031

The ordinary entrance-to-Cedar-Overlook walk is 2.6 km one way. The 12 May 2031, 09:00 entrance-board reading is 1.1 m; the ranger signed this as the reading for today's guided walk.

The group meets at the entrance shelter at 09:15. Distances describe the walking route, not straight-line separation. The guided group uses the same published closure rules as other visitors.

## A route, not a loop
During the Alder Footbridge closure, walkers reach the Cedar Overlook by following the signed Mill Road bypass from marker M2 to marker M5. The bypass adds 0.8 km to the outward walk.

## Completing the walk
Return from the overlook using the same Mill Road bypass; the old east-bank spur is fenced for nesting birds and is not an alternative return route.
At 1.4 m or above, the Mill Road ford is closed too: turn back at M2; do not substitute the ford for the footbridge.

## Water condition attached to the bypass
The bypass is open only while the creek gauge is below 1.4 m.

## Getting into the foyer
For step-free entry to the afternoon performance, use the courtyard door on Birch Lane. The main High Street doors lead to six steps before the foyer; the courtyard route reaches the foyer by a level passage.

## Permission condition
The image can be included in the public river-history page only after the Rights Register marks R-42 as cleared for web publication.

## Initial temperature state
For an L7 camera running firmware 3.2, start a new dark library after changing the sensor target temperature. Set the target to −10 °C and allow 12 minutes after the displayed temperature first reaches that value.

## Reading the signs
Temporary bypass signs have an amber arrow and the word OVERLOOK. Permanent white posts still mark the original path, including its closed sections. A volunteer may be stationed at the entrance on weekends, but the absence of a volunteer does not cancel a closure notice.

The parser accepts a header row in any column order. Column order is useful for spreadsheet readability and does not change field meaning. Files downloaded from the example station include a comments column for maintenance notes, which the export omits. Comments can contain commas when quoted normally.

# Public session card — 7 February 2032

Tonight's science frames use 90 s exposures. Keep this duration for the dark series; do not apply the older 60 s classroom example.

The camera is an L7 with firmware 3.2. A guide has just changed its target from −5 °C to −10 °C. The red-light room opens at 19:00.

## File naming and reuse
Store the combined master under dark/L7_f32_m10_<seconds>s.fit, replacing <seconds> with the exposure duration as an integer. Do not reuse a master made at −5 °C.

The demonstration target is a bright emission nebula. Its catalogue name appears on the finder chart, but participants do not need to enter that name into calibration software. Calibration records use the instrument, firmware, temperature and duration rather than a target name.

## Initial temperature state
For an L7 camera running firmware 3.2, start a new dark library after changing the sensor target temperature. Set the target to −10 °C and allow 12 minutes after the displayed temperature first reaches that value.

## Records retained off the public page
Keep capture logs and internal handling notes with the accession record according to the archive's retention process. The public page does not need internal scanner identifiers, staff shift notes, or the physical storage shelf code to give a visitor the supported image and its approved credit.

# DrizzleCSV demonstration job 18

Job configuration:
```json
{"station":"RQ2","timezone":"UTC+02:00","adapter_version":4}
```
Input rows:
```csv
observed_at,reading
2031-06-08T10:15:00,-9999
2031-06-08T10:20:00,0
```

UTC+02:00 is a fixed offset in this synthetic job; no seasonal-clock rule is needed. The two displayed rows are complete.

## Reading semantics
Convert the literal reading value -9999 to JSON null and set quality to "missing".

# DrizzleCSV adapter contract, version 4
This synthetic contract describes a small weather-station exchange format. Version 4 is current for the demonstration dataset.
The value 0 is a valid measurement and must remain numeric zero; an empty reading cell is a row-validation error, not the -9999 missing-data code.

The directory also contains flat-field examples from previous lessons. Flat frames correct uneven illumination; their labels should not be copied into the thermal calibration record. The examples remain available to explain the difference between calibration types, not to prescribe this evening's exposure time.

## Output shape
The exported object uses these exact keys:
```json
{"observed_at_utc":"ISO-8601 Z time","reading":0,"quality":"measured","station":"site code"}
```
For a nonmissing numeric reading, quality is "measured".

There is no additional confidence field and no wrapper named data. A consuming application may place several exported objects inside its own array, but that application's container is not part of the single-row conversion contract. Preserve the distinction when creating test fixtures or explaining one row to an operator.

Each CSV file belongs to one station, even when an operator has copied the file into a folder named for a regional campaign. Use the station value from the job configuration. Folder names help a person organize uploads but do not become exported station identifiers.

The unit selected by a station is documented in its registration record. This adapter does not silently rescale units, round the numeric reading, or append a unit suffix to the JSON number. Downstream chart labels may display units separately. A failed row is reported with its physical CSV line number.

## Reproducibility
Record the adapter version in the batch manifest, not inside each exported measurement. A manifest can also include the filename and a checksum. Those fields establish batch provenance and should not be copied into an individual measurement object merely because they appear beside it in a log.

# Blue Lantern lot BL-31

Lot BL-31 may be offered for lending only if at least 80% of its viability sample germinates. The recorded untreated sample has 15 roots at least 5 mm long on day 10; one additional seed has a 3 mm root.

The lot was tested with the 20-seed P-6 method. No seeds in this sample were nicked or soaked.

After scoring, place the tested seeds in the compost container. Do not return them to a lending envelope even if a seed has no visible root. The remaining untested lot should stay dry in its labelled jar until the librarian has entered the result and decided whether the lot may be offered.

A swelling seed is not yet a scored germination. The photo guide shows several stages because visitors often want to understand the process. Only the stage stated in this protocol counts toward the recorded viability result; photographs are illustrative and do not change the timing requirement.

Use a pencil to label the box with the variety, lot code, and start date. Ink on a loose paper label can run in the damp chamber. The label helps volunteers keep similar-looking peas apart; the box's shelf position is not an identifier and may change when the room is cleaned.
Nicking and soaking may be appropriate for a separate planting trial, but pretreated seeds cannot be substituted into the untreated viability sample or its recorded percentage.

## Score at a consistent time
Count a seed as germinated only when its root is at least 5 mm long. Record the final count on day 10, not the first day on which any root appears.
The neck loop works with a hearing aid set to its T-coil program; an ordinary Bluetooth pairing mode will not connect to this system. Headphones are available for visitors without a T-coil aid.

# Dated audience notice: 16 November matinee

For the 16 November 2031 matinee, curtain is at 14:00 and the courtyard door and access desk open at 13:15. The usual 13:30 opening is replaced for this performance because the access team is offering receiver familiarization.

The performance uses the standard neck-loop system for rows A–F. The programme running time is 95 minutes including a short interval.

## Assisted listening
Borrow a neck-loop receiver from the access desk for seats in rows A–F.

# Willow Room Theatre — audience access guide
Public access edition, November 2031. This fictional theatre has one auditorium and one courtyard entrance.

The demonstration target is a bright emission nebula. Its catalogue name appears on the finder chart, but participants do not need to enter that name into calibration software. Calibration records use the instrument, firmware, temperature and duration rather than a target name.

Breakfast tickets help the volunteers count how many portions to prepare. A ticket is valid for either the standard plate or the listed alternative, subject to availability. Visitors do not need to explain a medical history to exchange a ticket for a sealed cup or ask to see an ingredient label.

# Workshop glaze notice — current

Guest-workshop pieces marked GL-9 must stay out of C17: that glaze batch requires a separate cone-5 firing with no top hold. All other pieces already approved on the C17 load sheet keep the SLOW-6 plan.

GL-9 is an invented studio glaze code. This sign is public so participants can identify the affected workshop work.

## Selected profile
For load C17, select the studio's SLOW-6 profile and program a 20-minute hold at the top temperature. The profile's controlled cooling segment ends at 900 °C.

## Identification after firing
Mark each C17 box with the firing date and the literal batch label C17-S6-H20. The label records the profile and top hold, not an artist's name or a glaze recipe.

Glaze names are recorded on individual test tabs in the load folder. A public workshop sign may add a special rule for a particular glaze batch. Read a glaze exception together with the current load plan before deciding which pieces may be included in a firing; a shared clay body alone does not settle compatibility.

# Studio firing plan — C17
Synthetic private owner notebook. All names, codes, and work described here are invented for this benchmark.

## Unloading condition
Keep the kiln closed until its display is below 80 °C before unloading C17.

Use a pencil to label the box with the variety, lot code, and start date. Ink on a loose paper label can run in the damp chamber. The label helps volunteers keep similar-looking peas apart; the box's shelf position is not an identifier and may change when the room is cleaned.
The earlier 120 °C unloading shortcut applies only to unglazed test tiles; C17 contains glazed bowls and does not qualify for that shortcut.

The shelves have been brushed and checked for drips. Shelf numbers are maintenance labels; they do not indicate which profile a load should use. The kiln room's wall chart illustrates several firing curves for classes, including profiles that are not appropriate for this particular load.

## Communicating accurately
Staff should repeat the event's ingredient and handling information without guaranteeing that a meal is safe for a particular person's allergy. The visitor can read the sealed cup's manufacturer label before deciding whether to accept it.

## Listed alternative
At the 9 June community breakfast, the sealed oat cups labelled O-4 are the listed option made without peanut ingredients. Hand the cup to the visitor unopened, together with a fresh wrapped spoon.

## Shared equipment limitation
Do not describe any item prepared on the shared toast counter as peanut-free.

The toaster, tongs, and spreading board are shared with peanut-butter toast; removing a topping or wiping a visible crumb does not turn that service into the sealed-cup option.

# Public menu availability — 9 June

The O-4 sealed-cup stock for 9 June is 18 cups, reserved at the serving desk rather than on the toast counter. Service runs from 08:30 to 10:00, or until the relevant item runs out.

The stock notice describes initial quantities, not a live count. The serving lead can confirm remaining cups during the event.
